glyph_origin: Two possible interpretations: • Ideogram (指事) – three small dots > small. • Pictogram (象形) – three granules of sand – original character of 沙 > small. Starting from some bronze inscriptions, the dots have become elongated. Based on this form, Shuowen erroneously considers it to be an ideogrammic compound (會意): 八 (“to divide; to separate”) + 丨 (“small object”). Compare with 少, represented by four dots in its oracle bone script form. Unrelated to the bottom part of 京, 示, 尞, 尗, and 原.
